tasks.task: Build a programme with trades in site order

items.when: When a job is won or a contractor chosen and the start date is set
When you have the scope, trade list and start date and need tasks, durations, links and key dates
When the job could run in one go or in phases, to compare two plans with money and dates
Before a finish date is promised, to test it against the crews and hours really free
When trades overlap, to check each handover between them and what gives way in a clash
When durations look hopeful, to compare them with how long past jobs really took

tasks.task: Write the two-week look-ahead for trades

items.when: Every week on site, to tell each trade what is coming and catch what will stop them
When the look-ahead must be drawn from the current programme and what moved this week
When the same tasks slip week after week, to trace where the work waits and why
When trades wait on each other, to look at the handoffs and try one small fix

tasks.task: Turn site notes into a daily site report

items.when: Every site day and every week, to know which record is due and when
When you have rough notes, voice memos and a photo list and need the report under fixed headings
When the notes are a voice recording and need a written transcript first
When a delivery note, meter or sign was photographed and its text must go in the report
When voice memos must be turned into text on the site manager's own computer

tasks.task: Keep the delay and weather log

items.when: When a delay happens, to log date, cause, activity, days lost and the record that proves it
Each week, to see where work waited, the trend and whether the fix is working
When one kind of delay keeps coming back, to chase the cause and a way to prevent it
Before the log supports a claim, to tie each entry to a dated note, photo or message

tasks.task: Write the weekly client progress report

items.when: Every week on a live job, to give the client one page with bad news first and decisions due
When you want a shorter version built from done, stuck and needed, to compare
When the week had a setback, to state the loss, the numbers and the next step briefly
When the client asks if the job is on budget and on time, to work out the cost and time position
Before sending, to have a fresh reviewer read it as the client paying for the job

tasks.task: Write a renovation brief every builder can price the same way

items.when: When an owner plans a renovation and needs a room-by-room brief for builders to quote on
When the budget may not stretch, to compare the full job with a phased one, with money and dates
When the brief lists finishes but not how the rooms will be used day to day
When the brief is drafted, to have a fresh reviewer read it as a builder who must price it

tasks.task: Compare builders' quotes like for like

items.when: When three quotes do not match and you need them set against the brief line by line
When the quotes must go side by side in one table before you judge them
When deposit terms and lead times differ, to compare risk and how safe each deposit is
When each quote comes with its own contract, to get a cost and risk table across them
When two or three quotes are close, to have a fresh reviewer pick one against the brief

tasks.task: List the questions to ask contractors before hiring

items.when: When quotes are in and the owner needs questions on exclusions, allowances and payment stages
When the owner will phone past clients, to get fair questions and a sheet to record answers
When a builder asks for a large deposit, to score how safe it is and what terms to ask for

tasks.task: Read the building contract in plain words before signing

items.when: When the builder sends a contract, to see what each side owes and the risky clauses
When terms on payment, delay or defects look one-sided, to flag them and when to call a lawyer
When the contract is long, to rate the key clauses and risks by how serious they are

tasks.task: List pre-start duties, permits and inspections

items.when: Before work starts, to list who holds each safety role and which documents and permits must exist
When the whole set-up, from contract to first day on site, must happen in order
When it is not clear which approvals the work needs, to list the rules and risk areas to check

tasks.task: Write RFIs and keep the RFI and submittal registers

items.when: When a drawing, spec or site condition raises a question the documents do not answer
When you need the RFI log and a submittal register with submit-by dates worked back
When answers are overdue, to pull every open question from notes and emails into one chase list

tasks.task: Check a variation and control the change

items.when: When a request, instruction or site condition may change the work, price or time
When the change must be written up with its cost, its time effect and who approved it
When a variation is claimed, to check it against the signed contract and its prices
When variations keep coming, to check each one's cost and time against the contract
When the client asks for extra work, to set out the options and draft the reply

tasks.task: Check a payment claim or a funding draw

items.when: When a payment falls due and must match the work done and the changes agreed
When a builder's invoice arrives, to recalculate each line and total and list what is missing
When several invoices arrive, to match them to orders and list amounts to query
When a lender funds the build, to plan how each period's costs are paid from equity and loan
When build costs or draw dates change, to recheck interest and any funding shortfall

tasks.task: Track cost against budget on a live job

items.when: When you have budget, programme and spend to date and need a forecast finish cost
When payments in and out must be forecast for the next 30, 60 and 90 days
When the cost sheet has grown by hand, to catch formula errors and broken links

tasks.task: Write a calm, firm letter to a contractor about a problem

items.when: Before writing, to get the facts of the dispute into one sheet with dates
When there are delays, poor work or a price above the quote and the owner wants it in writing
When the first letter got no reply, to try a version where a no still moves things on
When a call or site meeting comes first, to plan an opening, calm questions and a fallback
When the problem has become a formal dispute and needs a dated timeline and a demand draft
When the owner is angry, to sum up the builder's side first and ask how the fix will work
Before sending, to tie each fact in the letter to a dated message, photo or contract clause

tasks.task: Write site meeting minutes and chase the actions

items.when: When you have rough notes and need decisions, actions with owners and dates, and open questions
Each week, to check last week's open actions and set the next agenda
When the meeting must fit the weekly cycle of look-ahead and client report

tasks.task: Keep the client's decisions and approvals on record

items.when: At the start, to agree channels, update days and where decisions and approvals are recorded
Each week, to list the decisions the client owes and the date each is needed by
When decisions are scattered across messages, to pull them into one dated list

tasks.task: Build the snag list and the handover pack

items.when: When inspection records must become a defects register with owners and proof of closure
When the owner or the maintenance team takes over and needs a note to run from
At the end, to show what was delivered and accepted, with a register

tasks.task: Record a site incident and tighten the procedure

items.when: On the day, to record what happened, when and who was told, in the daily report
Afterwards, to write a blameless report, a safer procedure and tracked prevention actions
When the same kind of incident repeats, to test the chain of causes against the facts

tasks.task: Price a small job and write the quote

items.when: When you have call notes and photos and need a costed quote in your own template
When the job uses boards or panels, to plan cuts that waste the least material
When quantities come from measurements, to check the units and the margin for error
When you could price it two ways, such as fixed or staged, to have a fresh reviewer pick

tasks.task: Run a close-out review and capture the lessons

items.when: Before the review, to pick the format, the numbers to pull and who hears the lessons
When the job is done, to run a review that keeps blame out and turns lessons into rules
When there is no time for a meeting, to get a one-page note of what to repeat and change

always.when: Before any report, letter or register goes out, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the job needs layouts, finishes and a design brief, not only a build scope
When the site needs risk assessments, method statements or a safety plan written
When materials must be sourced, ordered and tracked against lead times
When the building contract needs a full plain summary and a list for a lawyer
When job costs and payments must be recorded and matched to the bank
When the finished building needs a maintenance schedule after handover

gaps: The library is thin for this role: about 55 items fit, and most site paperwork rests on the kit alone
No library item builds a construction programme, sequences trades or draws a critical path or bar chart
No library item writes a daily site report, a look-ahead or a delay and weather log
No library item estimates building costs or takes off quantities from drawings
No library item writes RFIs or keeps a submittal register
No library item prepares a builder's payment claim with stage values, retention and variations
No library item writes a risk assessment, method statement, site induction or toolbox talk
No library item covers permits, building control stages or inspection bookings
No library item drafts a delay notice or an extension of time claim from the delay log
No library item plans long-lead material orders against the programme
No library item writes a subcontract scope or a trade package
No library item builds a room-by-room snagging checklist or a handover pack with warranties and manuals
No library item offers different build sequences to compare for one job
